positions.as_written: Assess all four factors in every patient, because the pattern decides the operation.
Expect a soft tissue reconstruction alone to work best where the skeletal factors are normal.
Grade recurrence risk after a first dislocation by the factors present rather than by the severity of the event.
State which indices are soft, because quoting a threshold as a cutoff overstates it.
Patellar height ratios disagree systematically, so the ratio must be named with the number.
Decide whether the dominant problem is vector or restraint, because that choice selects the operation.
Record the knee position at which the tubercle to groove distance was acquired.
Address two mild factors in preference to overcorrecting one, which matches both the mechanics and the reported outcomes.

Take the patient's age, physiology, comorbidities, knee demand, psychological state and their own ideas, concerns and expectations into the decision, because the indices describe a knee and the operation happens to a person.
